lines.text: Vanguard, 2026: the most common match maxes out at 3%.
lines.say: Vanguard, twenty twenty-six: the most common match maxes out at three percent.

lines.text: It's written "50% up to 6%," and the 50 isn't what it sounds like.
lines.say: It's written fifty percent up to six percent, and the fifty isn't what it sounds like.

lines.text: On a hypothetical $60,000 salary, 6% is $3,600, and the employer adds half: $1,800.
lines.say: On a hypothetical sixty thousand dollar salary, six percent is thirty-six hundred, and the employer adds half, eighteen hundred.

lines.text: Put in 3% instead, and the match drops to $900.
lines.say: Put in three percent instead, and the match drops to nine hundred.
That's nine hundred dollars a year unmatched.

lines.text: The IRS safe harbor match: 100% of the first 3%, plus 50% of the next 2%, so 4% max.
lines.say: The IRS safe harbor match is a hundred percent of the first three percent, plus half the next two, so four percent max.

lines.text: Fidelity's average employer contribution was 4.8% of pay as of June 2026.
lines.say: Fidelity's average employer contribution was four point eight percent of pay as of June twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: The catch is vesting. Workers' own money is always theirs; a regular match can take up to 3 years, or 6 if graded.
lines.say: The catch is vesting. Workers' own money is always theirs; a regular match can take up to three years, or six if graded.

lines.text: The real number is rate times cap: 50% times 6% is 3%.
lines.say: The real number is rate times cap: fifty percent times six percent is three percent.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: "50% up to 6%" sounds generous. It maxes out at 3%
post.ig:
The most common 401(k) match, "50% up to 6%," maxes out at 3% of pay (Vanguard How America Saves 2026).
Hypothetical $60,000 salary: putting in 6% ($3,600) gets a $1,800 match; putting in 3% ($1,800) gets $900.
The IRS safe harbor match (100% of the first 3% + 50% of the next 2%) maxes out at 4% of pay. Fidelity's average employer contribution was 4.8% of pay in Q2 2026.
Vesting: a worker's own deferrals are always theirs; regular matches can take up to a 3-year cliff or 6-year graded schedule.
Sources: Vanguard How America Saves 2026; Fidelity Q2 2026 Retirement Analysis; IRS.
News and education, not financial advice.
